class.name: AIHearingSensor2D
class.brief_description: Event-driven 2D AI hearing with loudness, attenuation and temporary sound memory.
class.description: AIHearingSensor2D receives explicit gameplay noise events using [method report_noise]. It checks distance against hearing radius multiplied by sound loudness and a caller-provided attenuation factor, and stores the most recent perceived source position. The timer advances only when [method advance_time] is called. This class does not play audio, trace physics, identify teams or broadcast noise to other NPCs. To handle multiple listeners, create one instance per listener and deliver emitted sound events to interested sensors. The listener does not require visual line of sight.

method.name: report_noise
method.description: Reports a noise source. Loudness multiplies the base hearing radius. Occlusion is a caller-provided factor in [code][0, 1][/code] to attenuate sound across walls and other geometry. Returns [code]true[/code] if this listener heard the event, and records the position and loudness.

method.name: advance_time
method.description: Expires auditory memory using elapsed seconds (non-negative). Call every physics or fixed AI tick, even when no noise occurs.

method.name: has_sound_memory
method.description: Returns whether an accepted sound event remains in memory.

method.name: get_last_heard_position
method.description: Most recent audible event position; use [method has_sound_memory] to check validity.

method.name: get_last_heard_loudness
method.description: Loudness of the most recent accepted event.

method.name: get_memory_remaining
method.description: Seconds remaining until sound memory expires.

method.name: reset
method.description: Clears sound memory and the last remembered event.

method.name: set_hearing_radius
method.description: Sets the positive base listening radius.

method.name: set_memory_duration
method.description: Sets how long an accepted noise remains remembered; zero disables persistent memory.

members.member: Base hearing range, scaled by loudness and occlusion.
Seconds the most recent accepted noise remains remembered.
